title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s current hiring process, employee onboarding checklist, performance and feedback cycle guidance, and manager expectations. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers to ensure consistent, equitable, and scalable people practices.

Scope: Applies to full-time, part-time, and contractor roles at Redwood (US and EU entities). This document references our HRIS, ATS, and internal templates (see Related pages for links).

1) Hiring: process and decisions

Summary: Hiring at Redwood is a partnership between Hiring Manager, People Ops, Recruiting, and Interviewers. The objective is to hire for role fit (skills + culture), forecast capacity needs, and minimize time-to-offer while maintaining a high-quality candidate experience.

A. Requisition and approval (step-by-step)
1. Hiring manager drafts a role brief using the Role Brief Template (link in People Ops workspace). Include: job summary, outcomes in 6/12 months, required/desired skills, compensation band, interview rubric.
2. Submit requisition in Greenhouse with org code and hiring justification. Attach role brief.
3. People Ops reviews requisition for headcount, equity, and comp band. Approval turnaround: 48 business hours.
4. Finance confirmation if hiring above manager level or outside budget.

B. Interview loop design (standard templates)
- IC technical role (backend/inference/platform): Recruiter + 2 technical interviews (coding/architecture/ops), 1 system design, 1 cross-functional collaboration interview, final hiring manager + bar-raiser panel.
- Product/PM role: Recruiter + 1 product sense interview, 1 execution/estimation exercise, 1 stakeholder collaboration interview, final leadership interview.
- Non-technical roles (Design/Go-to-market/Customer Success): Recruiter + 1 role-skill interview, 1 culture-fit interview, final manager interview.

Interviewer instructions (required):
- Use the published interview rubric attached to every open job.
- Ask behavioral questions tied to outcomes in the role brief.
- Score independently in Greenhouse within 48 hours.
- Disclose any conflicts of interest to People Ops.

C. Candidate evaluation and offer
1. Hiring debrief: Hiring manager convenes interviewers within 3 business days of final interview. Document consensus and dissenting feedback in Greenhouse.
2. Compensation: People Ops provides final comp range and equity calculation. For exceptions, prepare a written rationale and finance approval.
3. Offer: Recruiter issues offer letter using the Offer Letter Template. Candidates get 72 hours to respond (flexible per role).
4. Negotiation: Standard negotiation guidelines are in the Compensation FAQ. Any deviation requires People Ops approval.

D. Diversity, equity and inclusion checkpoints
- Require at least one diverse slate or a documented rationale when a diverse slate cannot be produced.
- Use structured interview guides to reduce bias.
- People Ops runs quarterly funnel and hiring conversion audits.

2) New hire onboarding: 30-60-90 day plan and checklist

Objective: Enable new hires to reach independent contribution quickly while feeling welcomed and connected to team and company culture.

A. Pre-boarding (before day 1)
- People Ops: creation of official offer packet, benefits enrollment links, and first-week schedule.
- IT: device provisioning (laptop, monitors, VPN account), accounts (Slack, Google Workspace, HRIS) created at least 3 business days before start.
- Manager: First-week agenda and team welcome note; assign onboarding buddy.

B. Day 1\u20137: orientation and admin
- Day 1: New hire orientation (People Ops) \u2014 company mission, org chart, benefits overview, security basics, code of conduct.
- Manager: 1:1 kickoff, review 30/60/90 outcomes, clear expectations, immediate priorities.
- Buddy: introductions, team norms, calendar shadowing.
- Checklist items: NDA signed, payroll set up, software licenses provisioned, baseline access validated.

C. Week 2\u20134: role ramp and integration
- Manager: weekly 1:1, assign first project with clear acceptance criteria, schedule cross-functional intro meetings.
- Learning: Training plan (internal docs + recommended external courses), access to repo readmes, and runbooks.
- People Ops: 30-day check-in survey; manager + People Ops meet if any concerns.

D. 30-60-90 objectives (example template)
- 30 days: Orientation complete; deliver a short knowledge-share; ship a small task with mentor sign-off.
- 60 days: Independently own a medium-scope task; present learnings to team.
- 90 days: Meet success criteria described in role brief; manager recommendation for continued growth.

E. Onboarding metrics and ownership (table)
| Item | Owner | Target 
| Device & accounts provisioned | IT | Day 0\u20132 
| Orientation completed | People Ops | Day 1 
| 30-day check-in completed | Manager + People Ops | Day 30 
| 90-day performance review | Manager | Day 90 

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Overview: Redwood operates on a quarterly growth cycle with continuous feedback. Formal evaluations occur twice per year (mid-year and annual). Managers are responsible for ongoing coaching, calibration, and documentation.

A. Continuous feedback practices
- Weekly 1:1s: Required for the first 6 months of new hire\u2019s tenure; thereafter cadence set by manager (at least bi-weekly).
- Feedback when observed: Use the praise/area-for-growth model and document in the performance system.
- 360 feedback: Optional for calibration and development planning.

B. Formal performance reviews (timeline)
- Mid-year review: manager assessment + self-review + optional peer feedback. Calibration meeting occurs within the business unit.
- Annual review: full cycle with calibration across teams, compensation adjustments, and promotion discussions.

C. Rating guidance and calibration
- Use a three-tier rubric: Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement. Avoid forced distributions; focus on narrative evidence.
- Calibration process: Managers submit written evidence; People Ops runs calibration sessions by level and function. Final decisions documented in HRIS and shared with employees in a one-on-one.

D. Performance improvement plan (PIP) and support
- Trigger conditions: sustained performance below expectations after coaching for two consecutive review cycles or immediate severe conduct failures.
- PIP structure: clear goals (SMART), timeline (typically 60\u201390 days), success criteria, regular checkpoints, and assigned mentors or training.
- Outcomes: Successful completion, extension with documented rationale, or separation. People Ops and Legal are consulted before any termination.

4) Manager guide: expectations and playbook

Core manager responsibilities:
- Hire and onboard: design interview loops, make timely decisions, and run structured onboarding.
- Develop and coach: weekly 1:1s, career conversations, and development plans.
- Performance management: timely feedback, fair assessments, and responsible calibration participation.
- People practices: prioritize psychological safety, inclusive decision-making, and equitable development opportunities.

Manager checklist (first 90 days of a new manager):
1. Complete Manager Fundamentals training (People Ops).
2. Read team role briefs and backlog—meet with each direct report for 1:1 and career goals.
3. Establish 1:1 cadence and team meeting rhythms.
4. Schedule a 30/60/90 check-in with your manager and People Ops.

One-on-one best practices:
- Use a shared agenda; alternate who sets the agenda weekly.
- Track action items and follow-ups.
- Balance operational items with development and wellbeing.

Coaching conversation template:
1. Observation: describe the specific behavior or outcome.
2. Impact: explain why it matters.
3. Inquiry: ask for the employee\u2019s perspective.
4. Next steps: agree on concrete actions and timelines.

5) Promotions, leveling, and compensation

Promotion process:
- Candidate nomination: Manager submits promotion packet with evidence (impact summary, examples mapped to level rubric, peer feedback).
- Calibration: People Ops facilitates level-by-level calibration.
- Compensation: Total comp adjustments are reviewed by Finance.
- Communication: Manager holds a private conversation with the employee and updates HRIS.

Leveling guidance:
- Use the published leveling rubric (technical and manager tracks). Evidence should map to the rubric competencies (impact, autonomy, technical breadth, leadership).

6) Offboarding and knowledge transfer

Standard offboarding steps:
1. Manager notifies People Ops and IT.
2. Exit interview scheduled by People Ops.
3. Knowledge transfer: document active work, handoff plan, and access revocation timeline.
4. Final payroll and benefits processes completed by Finance/People Ops.

8) Appendix: common questions and examples

Q: What is our standard notice period?
A: Standard notice is 2 weeks for ICs; managers and senior ICs often provide 4 weeks. Check local employment law for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

Q: How do we handle international hires?
A: People Ops coordinates with legal and local payroll partners; expect longer provisioning times (up to 3\u20134 weeks) for work permits or local entity hires.

Q: Escalation path for a difficult termination
A: Manager -> People Ops -> Legal -> Head of People Ops. Include documented performance history and all written warnings.

Document ownership and maintenance: This playbook is maintained by People Ops. Review cadence: annual full review and ad-hoc updates for policy or legal changes.

If you have suggested changes or a missed template, please file a People Ops request in the internal HR workspace or contact the author.
